title: Deciding Whether to Digitize a Family Business
paragraphs: Managing a family retail business built on decades of in-person customer relationships, Wardah faced considerable internal disagreement about whether shifting substantial operations toward online sales represented necessary adaptation or an abandonment of the personal service that had originally distinguished the business.

Her father, having built the business through direct relationships he considered essential to its identity, worried that digitization would sacrifice the very qualities that made the business genuinely distinctive within an increasingly impersonal commercial landscape.

Rather than treating this as an all-or-nothing decision, Wardah proposed a hybrid model, maintaining the in-person relationship-focused approach for existing loyal customers while cautiously exploring online channels specifically to reach new customers unlikely to discover the business otherwise.

Two years into this gradual, hybrid approach, the family business had expanded its customer base considerably through online channels while preserving the personal relationships that had originally sustained it, suggesting that thoughtful integration, rather than wholesale replacement, sometimes honored both innovation and inherited business values simultaneously.
